title: Grateful Dead Live at Fillmore Auditorium on 1967-05-05
lineage: SBD > unknown analog gens > DAT > CDR > EAC > SHN

ai_review.summary: Good‑quality early soundboard captures a high‑energy ’67 set highlighted by Golden Road, New Potato Caboose and Alligator.
ai_review.review: Despite the inevitable lo‑fi quirks of a 1967 tape—slightly bass‑heavy mix and occasional muddiness—the recording is clear enough to hear the band’s youthful fire.  The short four‑song set bursts with excitement, especially the tight Golden Road → New Potato Caboose transition and the face‑melting Alligator, making it a prized glimpse of early Dead evolution.

ai_rating.rationale: Average reviewer rating is 4.38/5; most comments praise the performance and deem the recording the best available for this era despite modest technical flaws.

recording_quality.technical_notes: Mix is a bit bass‑saturated and at times muddy, but instruments remain distinct; overall clarity is strong for a mid‑1967 board tape and considered the best source for this material.

standout_songs: He Was A Friend of Mine
show_quality.setlist_flow: A concise four‑song set that flows tightly—Golden Road into New Potato Caboose, then straight into Alligator—showing the band’s early knack for seamless transitions.

band_member_comments.Jerry: Repeatedly praised for fiery, on‑point guitar work and a powerful solo on He Was A Friend of Mine.
band_member_comments.Phil: Described as ‘having a ball’, with hot, prominent bass lines especially at the start of Alligator.
band_member_comments.Bob: Noted for strong three‑part vocal harmonies (Jerry, Bob, Phil) and solid rhythm guitar throughout.
band_member_comments.Keys: Pigpen’s organ work is highlighted – described as whizzing, B3‑rich, and a key part of the Alligator jam.
band_member_comments.Drums: Bill Kreutzmann (sometimes referenced as Bill Summers) receives credit for solid, artistic drumming; some listeners mention occasional mud but overall drives the set.
